result.title: Rethinking LLM-Guided Visual Question Answering: Does Deeper Knowledge Integration Really Help?
result.summary: Knowledge-based Visual Question Answering (VQA) requires reasoning that extends beyond visible image content, demanding external commonsense and factual knowledge. While recent work leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) as knowledge sources, the question of how deeply such guidance should be integrated into a vision language architecture remains underexplored. In this work, we generate structured reasoning guidance, visual focus concepts, distractor elements and external knowledge using Llama~3.3~70B and systematically compare two integration strategies within a unified frozen ViT + FLAN-T5 framework on the OK-VQA benchmark: decision level late fusion and attention-matrix injection. Contrary to the prevailing assumption that deeper integration is superior, we find that shallow late fusion achieves the strongest results (39.4% exact match, +10.0 over the no guidance baseline), outperforming deep attention modification (31.8%) under data scarce fine-tuning. We further contribute an LLM based augmentation pipeline that expands training data more than tenfold via question paraphrasing. Our findings indicate that integration depth must be matched to the data regime.

AI.brief_summary: 用 Llama 3.3 70B 生成结构化推理引导、视觉焦点概念、干扰项与外部知识，在冻结 ViT + FLAN-T5 上系统比较决策级 late fusion 与注意力矩阵注入两种整合深度；OK-VQA 上数据稀缺微调时浅层融合最佳（39.4% vs 31.8%），并附一套问题改写扩充训练数据的流程。
